title: Redwood April 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands. Maya opened with high level business metrics and hiring priorities. Luis gave infra and runtime updates including performance wins and a note about upcoming private deployment features. Priya covered product roadmap and Optimize toolkit changes. HR and finance shared hiring and budget context. Session ended with Q&A; several action items and follow-ups were recorded.
next_steps: Post recording and slides to internal wiki
Send consolidated Q&A doc to all employees
Department leads to submit hiring plans by 2026-05-06
Schedule product deep-dive session with SEs in early May

Ian Chen | Share infra benchmark spreadsheet (latency/cost) | 2026-05-01

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (host), Luis Ortega, Priya Kapoor, Ian Chen, Sam Torres, plus ~120 employees on call

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, wherever you are. Thanks for joining the April all-hands. We've got a packed agenda, um, high level numbers, product roadmap, and some org updates. Quick housekeeping  recording is on, ask questions in Q&A and we'll leave time at the end.

[00:28] Luis: Cool, I'll start with infra. Quick headline  we've rolled a new KV cache optimization into hosted, so customers are seeing roughly a 12 to 18% token-cost reduction on average for prefix-heavy workloads. There are still some edge patterns where the improvement is muted, but overall it's a win.

[00:52] Maya: Nice. Can you say a little about the rollout  was it hosted only or dedicated as well?

[01:04] Luis: It's staged  hosted rollout first, we validated with canaries last week, dedicated pools will get the same change but need a small runtime upgrade; that starts next week. There was one tiny regression in long-sequence tests that our team fixed overnight, so good catch by the bench team.

[01:30] Priya: On product side, we're shipping the initial Optimize recommendations UI next month. It'll surface batching, quantization, and cache suggestions per-route. The evals team has put together a small prompt set to track quality regressions; we'll tie alerts to that.

[01:52] Maya: Excellent  that aligns with our cost-aware performance theme. A quick business update: Q1 revenue beat plan by 8%, net churn is trending down, and usage growth is strong in mid-market. We still have some big enterprise deals in the pipe that could move the needle in Q2.

[02:12] Sam: On sales  pipeline is healthy. A few large POCs are in flight with regulated customers where Private deployment and dedicated SLAs are the gating items. We are asking security docs and KMS specifics this week.

[02:36] Maya: Great. HR note: we are prioritizing IC hiring for infra and product roles this quarter. We'll be conservative on non-engineering headcount given plan, but we will hire for critical roles that unblock product velocity.

[02:58] Ian: Regarding Private and on-prem, the upcoming release adds improved KMS integrations and per-tenant audit logs. There's still work on the on-prem installer to reduce friction; installer docs are getting a pass this sprint. The patch for the dedicated runtime will include the kernel selection improvements for attention kernels  that's the thing that reduced latency on some test suites.

[03:28] Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry can you repeat the kernel bit?

[03:34] Ian: Yeah, so we changed the default for attention kernel selection when sequences are >2k tokens; it now picks a lower-memory kernel which trades a little throughput for latency in worst-case sequences  helps customers with long context use-cases.

[03:54] Priya: We'll be updating model catalog docs to call out the default profiles and recommended quantization levels per model family. There's also a small UX change to show estimated unit cost per request in the console.

[04:14] Maya: Ops/observability update?

[04:18] Luis: Trace sampling defaults tightened up to reduce noise, and we're shipping a token-level cost breakdown in the console for per-route views. Alerting now ties to regressions from the evals harness, so if we see quality drift on critical prompts it'll generate a pager to SRE.

[04:40] Audience question (Q&A): "Will the Optimize recommendations be applied automatically or require manual opt-in?"

[04:48] Priya: Initially manual opt-in. We want customers to validate and control changes. Down the road we may offer an automated mode for enterprise customers with safeguards and a review window.

[05:10] Audience Q: "What about on-prem deployments and SOC 2?"

[05:14] Maya: We are pursuing SOC 2 and improving our compliance packages. For on-prem  customers who need extra controls can use Private with a customer-managed control plane. We're also working on ISO and more region-specific controls.

[05:36] Sam: Booking note  for deals that need a heavy security review, bring legal and security early; we have templates now that speed procurement.

[05:50] Priya: Quick demo snippet  (unmuted typing) okay pulling up the new Optimize UI. So you can see per-route recommendation, suggested batch sizes, cache TTLs and an estimate of tokens saved. The estimate has some variance, like plus/minus 10% depending on distribution, so we highlight that.

[06:18] Participant: Sorry, the demo lagged a bit on my side.

[06:22] Priya: Yeah, might be the stream. We'll post the video.

[06:30] Maya: Hiring  People Ops, can you remind folks of the internal referral bonus changes and timelines?

[06:36] Speaker 2 (People Ops): Yep, referral bonuses increased for hard-to-fill engineering roles, guidelines are in the hiring doc. We'll circulate a summary after the call.

[06:50] Ian: Small technical note  we've observed some GPU memory fragmentation in long-running Dedicated containers. The team has a mitigation that does periodic cache compaction; it's in canary and looks promising. If you have POCs that run long sequences continuously, talk to Infra, we can adjust node lifecycles.

[07:14] Audience Q: "Any changes to pricing or unit economics?"

[07:18] Maya: No broad price changes. We're focused on improving cost per token for customers by product improvements, not raising rates. For enterprise customers we'll continue offering commit/discount models.

[07:34] Luis: Also worth flagging  our new kernel selection plus prefix caching improvements together are what created the 12-18% improvement I mentioned earlier. Some customers on longer sequences see less uplift; we're iterating.

[07:52] Maya: Okay let's do a lightning round of wins and shout-outs.

[07:58] Luis: Shout-out to bench team for catching the long sequence regression.

[08:06] Priya: Shout-out to docs for the console copy updates.

[08:12] Sam: Shout-out to AE team for closing the three mid-market renewals this month.

[08:18] Maya: Thanks all. We'll end with Q&A  please upvote questions in the Q&A panel.

[08:28] Audience Q: "When will the dedicated runtime upgrade be available for partners?"

[08:33] Ian: Next week for early access to a subset of customers, GA in about three weeks pending canary results.

[08:46] Audience Q: "Is there a plan to support more model quantization formats?"

[08:50] Priya: Yes, roadmap includes broader quantization support and more automated suggestions in Optimize. We're tracking quality impact in the evals harness.

[09:04] Final notes: Maya: Thanks everyone  recording and slides will be posted. Department leads: submit hiring plans by 2026-05-06. We'll run a product deep-dive in early May; invites coming from product.

[09:28] (end)
